Second-Price Auction: Truth-Telling Is Dominant

This scene shows why honest bidding wins in a second-price auction. There is one opponent, and they bid honestly. Your bid does not set the price you pay. Winning means paying the opponent's bid. So bidding above your value gains nothing. It only creates wins that cost too much. Bidding lower throws away wins you could afford. As the formula below shows, the loss grows with the square of the gap. For example, your class auctions off one ⚽ ball. You value it at 6,000 won. A friend bids 4,000 won. Bid your honest 6,000 and you win. You pay only the friend's 4,000 💰 won. Bid 8,000 and the price stays the same. But if the friend had bid 7,000, you would overpay.
